key_insight: Separating appearance and motion using a 3D point-cloud control signal with multi-frequency positional encoding enables flexible, generalizable control over video generation in a task-agnostic way.
problem_solved: Provides a robust, interpretable alternative to ambiguous or task-specific control signals for video generation by explicitly decomposing and independently controlling appearance and motion dynamics.
method: Represent video dynamics as a 3D point-cloud control signal that encodes motion across space and time.
Apply multi-frequency positional encoding to the point cloud so both coarse and fine-grained motion patterns are captured and disambiguated.
Use an appearance–motion decomposition that can be plugged into existing generative pipelines (e.g., diffusion-based video models) to enable independent editing and flexible conditioning.
impact: Enables precise, reusable control primitives for video synthesis and editing, improving transferability across tasks and making interactive or conditional video generation more practical for practitioners.
visual_elements: High-level schematic: input (appearance + 3D point-cloud motion) → FlexAM decomposition → controllable video output.

Before/after comparisons or montage: generated videos with traditional signals vs. FlexAM-controlled outputs to highlight improved fidelity and controllability.
paper_title: FlexAM: Flexible Appearance-Motion Decomposition for Versatile Video Generation Control
paper_authors: Mingzhi Sheng, Zekai Gu, Peng Li, Cheng Lin, Hao-Xiang Guo
